summary.title: Visual Studio Code Can Do That?
summary.one_liner: A tour of lesser-known Visual Studio Code features and extensions for web and JavaScript developers, from font ligatures and Emmet to Prettier, Git integration, compound debug launch configs, Docker and Live Share.
takeaways: Enable font ligatures with Fira Code and the editor.fontLigatures setting to see symbols like => and === rendered as single glyphs.
Use keymaps and Settings Sync to carry shortcuts and configuration across machines and to share a team setup via a Gist.
Use Emmet, Intellisense in JSON and package.json, and //@ts-check to get more completion and type checking in plain JavaScript.
Configure Prettier with format-on-save, and debug front-end and Node.js servers together using a compound launch configuration.
Use the built-in Git tab, Docker extension, and Live Share for pair debugging without leaving the editor.
summary.summary: The article is a personal tour of Visual Studio Code features that the author found surprising after switching from other editors. It walks through setup steps with settings snippets and keyboard shortcuts, covering fonts, keymaps, Settings Sync, Emmet, JSON and JavaScript type checking, Prettier, the integrated terminal, Live Share, Git, and debugging. It ends with examples of running a zero-config Node.js debugger, column breakpoints, Docker tooling, and compound launch configurations for front-end and server debugging. The author's hands-on examples are the main content, and the piece was written when Live Share was in preview.
